questions.text: Which of the following numbers is an integer but not a whole number?

When a passage presents multiple perspectives and integrates statistical information, expert opinions, and case studies, the passage suggests that the reader should primarily do which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Memorize each statistic for recall.

options.label: B
options.text: Determine which perspective each piece of data supports.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore the author's stance and focus only on the data.

options.label: D
options.text: Treat all perspectives as equally valid.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Determine which perspective each piece of data supports..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the International Court of Justice (ICJ) from the International Criminal Court (ICC)?

options.label: A
options.text: ICJ prosecutes individuals for war crimes; ICC settles disputes between states.

options.label: B
options.text: ICJ settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions; ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and aggression.

options.label: C
options.text: Both courts are principal organs of the United Nations and are seated in The Hague.

options.label: D
options.text: ICJ has 124 states parties; ICC has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the General Assembly and Security Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: ICJ settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions; ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and aggression..

questions.text: A delivery company employs a driver who, while delivering a parcel, assaults the recipient because of a personal grudge unrelated to the delivery. The company’s policy prohibits violence. Applying the “course of employment” test for vicarious liability, is the company liable?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because the assault occurred during working hours and at the delivery location.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because the risk of assault is inherent in the business of serving the public.

options.label: C
options.text: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because the company had a policy prohibiting violence, which negates vicarious liability.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task..

questions.text: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established which limitation on Parliament's power under Article 368?

questions.text: A candidate encounters an inference question where one option is factually true in the real world but not supported by the passage. According to the Principle of Passage‑Only Reasoning, how should this option be treated?

options.label: A
options.text: Select it because it is factually correct

options.label: B
options.text: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage

options.label: C
options.text: Select it if it aligns with the candidate's domain knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: Mark it as correct only if the passage does not contradict it

questions.solution: Correct answer: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage.

questions.text: Concerning India's lunar exploration programme, which statement accurately reflects the outcomes of Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Chandrayaan-2 achieved a soft landing, while Chandrayaan-3 crashed on the lunar surface.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 achieved successful soft landings.

options.label: C
options.text: Chandrayaan-2's lander crashed, while Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither mission attempted a soft landing; both were orbiter-only missions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Chandrayaan-2's lander crashed, while Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing..

questions.text: In a principle-fact question, the principle requires "a voluntary act done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death." The facts show the accused pushed the victim during a sudden quarrel; the victim fell, hit his head, and died. The accused did not intend to kill. An answer option states: "The accused is liable because his act caused death." Which logical fallacy does this option exploit?

options.label: A
options.text: Denying the antecedent: it assumes that because the act was not intended to kill, it cannot be voluntary.

options.label: B
options.text: Affirming the consequent: it infers the presence of the required mental element (knowledge) solely from the occurrence of death.

options.label: C
options.text: Circular reasoning: it uses the conclusion (liability) as the premise for establishing the act was voluntary.

options.label: D
options.text: False dilemma: it presents only two extremes — either full liability or no liability — ignoring partial defences.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Affirming the consequent: it infers the presence of the required mental element (knowledge) solely from the occurrence of death..
